title: Buddhist, Indo-Islamic and Colonial Architecture

cards.b: Stupas, mosques, forts and Victorian railway stations are all part of the same story. UPSC wants you to date them and to name the style.

• Stupa: relic mound. Parts: anda (dome), harmika, chhatra, vedika, torana. Sanchi (Ashoka, later enlarged under Shungas and Satavahanas; torana gates), Bharhut, Amaravati, Sarnath (Dhamek).
  • Chaityas (prayer halls) and viharas (monasteries): Karle chaitya, Ajanta, Bhaja.
  • Ashokan pillars with lion capitals (Sarnath; national emblem).

Introduced the arch, dome, minaret and lime mortar, using the true arch. Phases: Slave (Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque, Qutb Minar, Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, Ajmer), Khalji (Alai Darwaza, Siri), Tughlaq (Tughlaqabad; sloping walls, Firozshah Kotla), Sayyid-Lodi (octagonal tombs, Lodi Garden). Provincial: Jaunpur (Atala Masjid), Gujarat (Jama Masjid, Ahmedabad; Sidi Saiyyed jali), Bengal, Malwa (Hoshang Shah’s tomb), Bijapur (Gol Gumbaz, with a very large dome).

• Babur: gardens. Humayun’s tomb (Delhi, 1560s, Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas; first garden-tomb, charbagh).
  • Akbar: Agra Fort, Fatehpur Sikri (Buland Darwaza, Jodha Bai palace, Panch Mahal; red sandstone), Akbar’s tomb at Sikandra.
  • Jahangir: Itimad-ud-daula (Nur Jahan; first use of white marble and pietra dura).
  • Shah Jahan: Taj Mahal (1632 to 1653, Ustad Ahmad Lahori), Red Fort, Jama Masjid, Moti Masjid.
  • Aurangzeb: Bibi ka Maqbara, Badshahi Mosque, Lahore.

Rajput forts: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Amber, Jaisalmer, Mehrangarh. Hill Forts of Rajasthan are UNESCO sites (2013). Deccan: Golconda, Daulatabad. Vijayanagara: Hampi (Vittala temple stone chariot; Lotus Mahal; Indo-Islamic mix). Sikh: Golden Temple, Amritsar (Guru Arjan Dev; Harmandir Sahib).

The Sultanate and Mughal forms blended with local craft: the chhatri, jharokha and jali are Indian elements.

• Early: Portuguese and French churches (Basilica of Bom Jesus, Goa), Danish Tranquebar.
  • Classical: Fort William (Calcutta), Government House.
  • Indo-Saracenic: Gateway of India, Victoria Memorial, Madras High Court (Robert Chisholm, F. W. Stevens).
  • Gothic: Victoria Terminus (Mumbai), University of Mumbai.
  • Imperial Delhi: Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker, New Delhi (1911 to 1931), Rashtrapati Bhavan, India Gate.

Le Corbusier’s Chandigarh (Capitol Complex is a UNESCO site since 2016); Louis Kahn (IIM Ahmedabad); Charles Correa (Gandhi Smarak, Jawahar Kala Kendra); Laurie Baker’s low-cost homes; B. V. Doshi (Pritzker 2018). The new Parliament building was inaugurated in May 2023 as part of the Central Vista project.

Thomas Metcalf (An Imperial Vision, 1989) argued that Indo-Saracenic was a style of empire: British rulers used Indian forms to show themselves as heirs to Mughals. Others stress craftsmanship by Indian workers and the hybrid creativity. The Central Vista debate echoes the old question of how power uses architecture.

The Taj Mahal, Red Fort, Qutb Minar, Humayun’s Tomb, Sanchi, Rani ki Vav (Gujarat), Victorian Gothic and Art Deco of Mumbai (2018) and Ahmedabad (2017, India’s first World Heritage City) show a living urban heritage. Conservation, ASI protected monuments and the Ancient Monuments Act 1958 are all in the news.

• “Mughal architecture synthesised Persian and Indian elements. Discuss.”
  • “Indo-Saracenic architecture—what and why?”
  • Prelims tip: Humayun’s tomb (charbagh), Itimad-ud-daula (pietra dura), Buland Darwaza (Akbar), Gol Gumbaz (Bijapur), Delhi Gate and India Gate (Lutyens).
